title: Virtual Executive Assistant
description:
I'm the founder of a digital growth marketing company that helps mission-driven founders scale their businesses with more ease & less overwhelm - and I'm looking for a small team of highly-skilled Executive Assistants to help take over the marketing and management tasks that make a huge difference in the lives of the people that hire us.



I'm looking for a max of 5 amazing executive assistants available for part-time (potential for full time) with a salary starting at $500 USD per month and with long term success and robust training, moving up to $700 USD per month as an emerging leader in the company.



If you have the following skill sets, I encourage you to apply:



REQUIRED EXPERIENCE:

- Minimum of 3–5 years of experience in Digital Marketing, Video Editing, Social Media Management, Content Creation, and Executive Assistant Work (Administrative Tasks, Calendar &
 Management, etc)

You’re trusted to manage marketing deliverables while providing high-level executive support, keeping priorities organized, systems moving, and leadership focused on growth instead of day-to-day execution. You've done it all from managing schedules to
 & calendar management. You have a meticulous eye for detail where Prioritization and Organization are your love language



- 1+ years of experience in Sales Funnels and Shopify

You're a professional who is passionate about helping changemakers simplify their lives by setting up systems that will allow them to operate their businesses with more ease and less overwhelm. You have experience with sales funnel and CRM software



- 1+ years of experience advertising on platforms like Instagram,
, Tik Tok, within a Marketing team consisting of Paid Acquisition, Organic Marketing, Customer Retention, & Product Marketing

You're an emerging leader who has the potential to head a team in the future that will report directly to you. Having leadership experience is a MAJOR plus



- Creating SOPs (Standard Operating Procedures)

You’ll ensure each business function has detailed documentation for repeatable and scalable growth if it isn't already place. If you see gaps, you take the initiative to fill them and produce results without anyone knowing there was an issue (yea, all that and a bag of chips :-)



- Experience working at a digital/online product/platform: You’re familiar with online courses, digital products & platforms and popular tools in the business space ranging from landing page builders and
 service providers to CRMs, and course hosting platforms aren’t foreign to you (We teach tools like Shopify, Convertkit, Kajabi, Teachable, Learnworlds, Calendly, etc)



ABOUT YOU:

- “You down with SOP? Yeah you know me!”—You’re an advocate for SOPs (Standard Operating Procedures) to make our systems repeatable & scalable.

- Your love language is processes & predictable, meteoric growth. We never question company progress towards the quarterly and yearly goals because you keep real-time metrics for all projects.

- You’re aware of new software and can look at current systems and identify how to automate tasks a company has been doing manually for months.

- You’re addicted to digital processes & automation in the world of social media because you love building connections in the digital space and you’ve seen how powerful it can be in business growth

- You’re driven by metrics & tracking. You know that you can’t improve something unless you measure it, so you develop ways to measure performance so your company is always predictably improving.

- Timeliness and deadlines are your jam. When we have a team call at 10:00am, you show up at 9:55am. When the deadline is Tuesday at 5:30pm, you have it done Monday.

- You overcommunicate clearly and confidently. If you agree/disagree with something, you communicate that without hesitation or overthinking. You’re no stranger to asking why we do things a certain way to ensure we’re intentional with our resources.

- You’re a leader and team player. Ego? What ego? If something needs to be done, you dive in to make sure all critical tasks are accounted and cared for.



If you’re nodding your head “Yes” to the above, proceed below to apply.



PERKS:

I'm committed to setting our staff up for success with access to trainings that will certify your skills in:

- Task & Calendar Management

- Launch/Sales Strategy Planning

- Sales Funnel Tech Setup (For E-Commerce or Service Based Businesses)

- Social Media Management

- Digital Media Marketing (Including
 and SMS Marketing)

- Lead Generation



After one week of training and assessment, you're officially certified under our internal training program, which means hitting the ground running with your new skills. Perks include:

- Part time work hours

- Work from anywhere in the world (as long as your internet signal is strong and computer is fast)

- Starting Salary at $500 USD a month ($6000 USD annual)

- Internal certification program to enhance your professional skills in your career (I have helped clients amass at least $10M from the same digital growth marketing strategies I will require you to learn)



Interested? Please reply to this post with the secret keyword "APPLES" so I know you can pay attention to detail - from there, I'll let you know next steps if you qualify.

 and video/phone

Compensation

We are willing to pay more for a candidate who already has meaningful California workers’ compensation experience and can contribute with minimal training.



There is significant opportunity for increased responsibility and growth for the right person.



IMPORTANT — How to Apply



Please begin your application with the words:



CALIFORNIA WC



Applications that do not include those words at the beginning may not be reviewed.



Please answer every question below in your application:

title: Accountant - Property Management
description:
Instructions:



1) Please take this survey as part of the application process for this position: 
/p/i7Koc8vtu75zd

2) Send a message describing your interest in the position



About the Role - Remote



About the Role

A US-based property management company is seeking a detail-oriented accountant to manage the books for several affiliated companies with residential real estate holdings. You'll own the full accounting cycle across multiple entities in a shared QuickBooks Online environment, produce investor reporting, and partner with our outside CPA at tax time. Experience with QBO and Buildium is preferred.



This is a remote role for someone who takes pride in books that are accurate, reconciled, and tie out cleanly — every month.



What You'll Do

- Manage full-cycle bookkeeping for multiple related LLCs (real estate holding companies plus a management company) within a combined QuickBooks Online file, separated by class.

- Own month-end close for each entity — bank and credit-card reconciliations, class-based adjusting entries, and review — producing a Balance Sheet by Class that ties for every entity, with no forced or "plug" entries.

- Maintain intercompany accounting — the "Due to / Due from" balances between the management company and each LLC — and reconcile them so they match on both sides.

- Administer centralized cash: record income and expenses collected/paid through the management company and allocate them to the correct entity by class.

- Prepare quarterly investor statements — distributions, capital accounts, property reserves, and loan/interest balances.

- Track property-level activity in Buildium (rents, operating expenses, tenant security deposits, reserves) and reconcile it to QuickBooks.

- Maintain loan and note schedules — mortgages, intercompany notes, and investor loans — including interest and amortization.

- Account for tenant security deposits and property reserves as proper liabilities, kept separate and never commingled.

- Handle AP/AR, owner distributions, and partner capital accounts.

- Partner with our outside CPA — deliver clean trial balances, tie-outs, and workpapers, and respond promptly to their questions.



What We're Looking For

- 3+ years of accounting/bookkeeping experience; real estate or property management experience strongly preferred.

- Strong QuickBooks Online skills, including multi-entity / class tracking — required.

- Solid grasp of accrual and cash basis, intercompany accounting, reconciliations, and LLC/partnership equity (capital accounts, distributions).

- Meticulous accuracy and a firm understanding that a balance sheet must balance for real reasons — you investigate differences rather than plug them.

- Self-directed and reliable in a remote setting, with clear written communication.

- Comfortable coordinating directly with an outside CPA firm.



Nice to Have

- Buildium experience · multi-entity real estate structures · intercompany reconciliation · investor reporting · strong Excel · relevant certification or degree.

title: Amazon & E-commerce Listing Designer (A+ Content / EBC), Canva + AI
description:
We're a US-based (Florida) fertilizer and soil mix company selling on Amazon and other e-commerce platforms. We're hiring a full-time, long-term Listing Designer to own the visual side of our product listings.



THE ROLE

You will design complete, sales-ready product listings, primarily for Amazon (gallery images + A+ Content / EBC), plus adapted versions for eBay, Walmart, Shopify, and other platforms.



For each product you will create:

- Main images

- Gallery images: lifestyle scenes and infographics (NPK, coverage, application, benefits)

- A+ Content

- Resized/adapted versions for eBay, Walmart, Shopify, and other marketplaces



Canva is our primary tool. All listings are assembled and finalized in Canva. AI image generation is welcome and encouraged for base assets, but AI is a helper, not a replacement for real listing design experience.



All listings are in English. You must be able to catch and fix typos, grammar mistakes, and awkward phrasing in any text that goes on your designs, and you must communicate with us clearly in English.



WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

- Proven experience designing Amazon listings and A+ Content (portfolio required)

- Strong Canva skills. This is your daily tool. Photoshop is a plus.

- Comfortable with AI image tools and able to refine AI output to a professional, sales-ready standard

- Strong written English: you catch copy errors, not just design

- Detail-oriented, reliable, follows instructions precisely

- Lawn/garden/fertilizer niche experience is a plus, not required



PAY: PER LISTING, NOT PER HOUR

We pay per completed listing. Our company policy is simple: we reward efficiency and quality. The faster you deliver work that meets our standard, the more you earn. Full-time workload (40 hrs/week). At a full-time pace, realistic earnings are $700 to $1,000+ per month. 



HIRING PROCESS

1. Interview for shortlisted applicants.

2. If selected: a PAID test task (one full listing set).

3. When finishing the paid test task, you sign our standard independent contractor agreement. This is company policy and standard procedure for everyone who works with us.



TO APPLY, READ CAREFULLY

Applications that don't follow these steps will be ignored:

1. Start your reply with the word "GREEN" so we know you read the full post.

2. Send your portfolio link (Amazon listings / A+ Content preferred).

3. List the design and AI tools you use. Canva is required. Tell us how long you've worked in it.

4. Tell us your fastest reliable turnaround for one full listing image set (main + 3 supporting + 1 A+ module).

title: Long-Form Historical Documentary Editor — Archive-First
description:
I’m hiring an editor for a serious, approximately 70-minute YouTube documentary about what happened to the Vanderbilt fortune.



The final narration, script, chapter structure and detailed visual plan are complete. The editor’s role is to source rights-cleared archive material and build the finished film.



The visual approach is:



* Authentic historical photographs, documents, maps, newspapers and engravings

* Genuine period film where it exists

* Restrained movement, evidence graphics and reusable visual systems

* No flashy “YouTube automation” style

* Absolutely no AI-generated images or video, synthetic archive footage, animated faces or fake historical recreations



Every visual and music asset must have an item-level source link and rights evidence suitable for commercial YouTube use. YouTube downloads, copyrighted documentary clips, watermarked media and unsupported “fair use” claims are not acceptable.



The selected candidate will first complete a genuine paid 2-minute-36-second Cold Open test. If successful, the full film will be delivered chapter by chapter.



To apply, begin your reply with VANDERBILT and provide:



1. Your two strongest relevant documentary or archive-based edits.

2. Exactly what you personally did on each example.

3. In 2–3 sentences, how you would verify and record commercial-use rights for one archive image and one music track.

4. Your editing software.

5. Your proposed turnaround for the test and full film.

6. Your best fixed all-in price for the paid test.

7. Your best fixed all-in price for the complete film.

8. Your price per finished minute for similar ongoing work.

9. What archive sourcing, music, revisions, project files and rights logging are included.

10. Every cost not included in your quote.

11. Whether the test fee is credited against the full-project price if hired.



State your currency clearly. Give the most competitive fixed price at which you can genuinely meet every requirement. Potential future documentaries may follow, but this is not guaranteed.
salary: fixed price, provide your best quote.

title: National Operations Support VA
description:
You must submit a CV, with a video please. 



We are seeking a highly organised and proactive National Operations Support VA to support our Operations team across multiple branches.



This is not a standard administration role. You will work closely with our National Operations Manager and State Operations Managers, helping monitor fleet compliance, operational performance, job documentation, scheduling pressures and day to day activities across the business.



The successful candidate will need to be confident following up outstanding actions, identifying issues before they become problems and communicating directly with managers and operational teams.



Working Days and Hours



This is a full time Tuesday to Saturday position.



The required shift is 8:30 am to 6:30 pm AEST, Tuesday to Saturday.



The shift includes:



One 15 minute break.

One 45 minute lunch break.

Breaks are to be taken at pre scheduled times to ensure consistent operational coverage throughout the day.



This equates to 45 working hours per week, excluding the scheduled breaks.



Tuesday to Friday will focus primarily on national operational monitoring, compliance, fleet management and reporting.



Saturday will have a greater focus on supporting live removal operations, responding to crew enquiries and ensuring Removal Contracts and operational documentation are properly completed.



Mandatory Prerequisites



Applicants must meet all of the following requirements to be considered for this role:



Previous experience working within the removals or logistics industry.

A practical understanding of operational environments, including scheduling, vehicles, crews, job movements and day to day logistics.

A dedicated work from home office or workspace suitable for full time professional work.

A workstation with a minimum of two computer screens.

A strong, stable and reliable internet connection capable of supporting cloud based systems, calls and online meetings throughout the working day.

Availability to work Tuesday to Saturday, 9:00 am to 7:00 pm AEST consistently.



Please do not apply if you do not have previous removals or logistics experience, or if you do not have an appropriate work from home setup.



Reporting To



The role reports directly to the National Operations Manager and works closely with our State Operations Managers nationally.



Key Responsibilities

Fleet and Compliance

Review daily vehicle inspection submissions and identify missing or incomplete inspections.

Report required follow up actions to the relevant State Operations Manager.

Monitor national fleet servicing requirements and upcoming service dates.

Coordinate servicing schedules between external mechanics and branch managers.

Monitor Container Weight Declaration requirements for container vehicles.

Prepare Safe Driving Plans for long distance removal work.

Coordinate quarterly depot inspections and report identified non conformances.

Operational Monitoring

Review branch calendars against available crews and vehicles to identify potential overbooking or capacity issues.

Raise concerns with Operations and respond to Sales enquiries regarding days where operational capacity appears tight.

Monitor permitted onsite times for fixed price and interstate removal jobs.

Notify field teams of expected job timeframes.

Identify and report jobs exceeding expected timeframes.

Assist with weekly branch performance scoring and operational reporting.

Crew Performance and Quality Control

Liaise with Operations Managers regarding employee and crew performance.

Maintain staff performance scores within our internal systems.

Review the previous day's completed jobs using a defined three point quality control process.

Check the quality and completeness of inventories and operational documentation.

Report identified quality issues to the relevant State Operations Manager.

Documentation and Systems Compliance

Monitor required forms submitted through our operational systems.

Check that the correct documentation has been completed for each job type.

Live Operations Support

About You

What Success Looks Like

title: Funnel Builder & Meta Ads Operator (SamCart/Unbounce + Ads Manager) - Part-Time to Full-Time
description:
We run a portfolio of digital product brands (parenting, finance, wellness) built on one repeatable system: organic content engines plus cold paid traffic, both converting through landing pages, checkout pages, and ascending product ladders.

We are hiring ONE person to run both ends of the conversion machine: build the pages, run the ads.

What makes this seat unusual: you inherit a finished system. The copy is written for you. The product images are generated for you. A paid video course (we give you access) is the exact playbook for both the pages and the campaigns. The offers, prices, and brand rules are fixed. Your job is precision execution: assemble, wire, launch, track, iterate. If you want creative freedom, this is the wrong seat. If you love following a proven system exactly and watching numbers move, keep reading.



THE WORK

1. Build landing and checkout pages in SamCart and Unbounce from finished copy, mockups, and reference layouts. (If your experience is GHL, Systeme, or Funnelish, that is fine; the builders all speak the same language.)

2. Set up tracking that tells the truth: pixel, conversion events, UTMs, GA4.

3. Launch and manage Meta cold-traffic campaigns per the course playbook: campaign structure, budgets, kill rules, scaling, inside an approved budget on our card.

4. Iterate pages against campaign data. The ad and the page are one machine; you run both ends.

5. Report weekly: spend, cost per purchase, ROAS, and your reading of what to do next.



PAY AND PATH

Part-time trial first (roughly 20 hrs/week, $400 to $600/month depending on evidence): complete the course, build the pre-launch infrastructure, assemble the first funnel's pages. When campaigns launch (expected within the quarter), the seat converts to full-time salary. Paid reliably twice monthly.



HOW TO APPLY (read carefully; applications missing any item are not reviewed)

Start your application with the word CONVERSION so we know you read this.

1. Ad accounts you have PERSONALLY run: monthly spend levels, cost per result, and one story of what you did when a campaign broke. Anonymised numbers are welcome.

2. Three pages YOU built: links or screenshots. Any platform.

3. Three sentences about a campaign you killed: what the numbers said and why you pulled it.

Shortlisted candidates get a small PAID test task ($75, about two hours), then a screen-share walk-through of an ad account you have managed, then a conversation with the principal.

title: Project Manager - Task Driver for US Agency - Chasers Only

3+ years managing projects or teams for an agency or online business.

Competent (not expert) in basic graphic design, video editing, social media posts, and document editing. Name your tools.

One story of a project you rescued by chasing people, with the result.



Our culture in one line: done means the client can click it, tasks have one owner and one date, and hours follow delivery. Reliable people get more hours, not less.

title: INBOUND APPOINTMENT SETTER — HAIR SALON (WARM FACEBOOK/INSTAGRAM LEADS, $1,250–$2,000/MO OTE + 13TH MONTH PAY)
description:
READ THIS FIRST



We're hiring ONE full-time Inbound Appointment Setter to call warm leads from our
 and Instagram ad campaigns for a color-specialist hair salon in Fontana, California.



This is NOT cold calling. Every lead you speak to has already raised their hand by submitting their info through one of our ads. Your job is to reach them fast, build trust quickly, understand what they actually want, and guide them into a booked appointment.



This role demands two things at once: sharp conversational judgment AND tight process discipline. The conversations are where you win or lose the booking. The process — cadences, call dispositions, CRM hygiene, follow-up tasks — is what makes the whole system work and what lets us measure anything. You need both. People who are great at one and sloppy at the other don't last here.



On the conversation side, what we're really hiring for is the ability to think on your feet. Someone replies three days later with just "sorry, been busy." Someone says they want highlights but describes something else entirely. Someone says "that's a bit far for me" but what they really mean is they don't see why it's worth the drive. If you can read what people actually mean and move the conversation forward without being told what to say next, you'll do well here.



If you need to be spoon-fed a script for every situation, this won't work.



IF YOUR BACKGROUND IS PRIMARILY CUSTOMER SERVICE OR VIRTUAL ASSISTANT AND NOT SALES, PLEASE DO NOT APPLY.



OTE: $1,250–$2,000/month (base $900–$1,000 + uncapped performance bonuses).

13th month pay included — paid every December, on top of your base. Not baked in. Not restructured. A full extra month of base pay, added on top.



---



ABOUT THE COMPANY



You'll be employed by Midnight Siren, a growth and client acquisition company that operates and supports beauty service businesses. Your day-to-day work focuses on a family-owned, color-specialist hair salon in Fontana, California that has served the Inland Empire for over 21 years.



The salon has 4.9 stars on Google with 200+ reviews and a stylist team with 75+ combined years of experience. The business is real, established, and respected in its market.



You'll work directly under Ethan, the founder of Midnight Siren — no middle managers, no agency layers between you and the person making decisions. The Midnight Siren team is small and tightly focused. The stylists at salon handle the in-salon experience; you and Ethan handle everything that gets a client booked.



A note on team structure: you will be the only appointment setter on the team. Your day-to-day working relationship is directly with Ethan. There are no peer-level coworkers, no team chat with other appointment setters, no group energy to feed off. If you thrive with autonomy, clear systems, and a direct manager relationship, this works well. If you need a team environment or peer social dynamic to stay motivated, this will feel isolating over time.



We're in an active scaling phase. Core processes exist and are being refined. They don't change daily, but they evolve as we learn. If you like improving systems alongside a team, you'll fit. If you want a fully crystallized corporate environment where nothing ever shifts, you won't.



---



WHAT YOU'LL ACTUALLY BE DOING



This is a front-line revenue role, not customer support.



Daily:



- Call new
/Instagram ad leads within minutes of opt-in (speed matters — you'll have task notifications throughout the day)

- Run our call script for the structured parts of the call, and use our frameworks + your own judgment for discovery and objection handling. The script covers the greeting, the offer, pricing, and the booking ask. Discovery can't be fully scripted — clients say what they say, and you'll need to adapt in real time.

- Respond to inbound SMS,
 
, and Instagram DMs that get escalated to a human when our AI can't handle them

- Collect cards on file via secure link (never over the phone), book appointments, reschedule, and cancel

- Call no-shows to get them back on the calendar

- Coordinate with stylists about client requests and scheduling needs

- Create follow-up tasks in HighLevel (our CRM)

- Submit a brief end-of-day report with your numbers



Weekly:



- One coaching/review call with Ethan (~30–45 min)

- Async coaching via Loom video reviews on your live call recordings between meetings

- Review your KPIs, own your numbers, and bring data-backed ideas to improve them



During training (first 2–4 weeks):



We'll meet daily for live coaching to get you fully ramped before transitioning to the weekly + async cadence.



---



A WORD ON THE CALL SCRIPT (READ CAREFULLY)



We use a script. We also need you to think.



Where the script is fixed: the greeting, how we introduce the salon, how we present the offer, how we state pricing, the booking ask, and our core objection responses. These are tested and they work. You run them as written. Your tone, warmth, and pacing are what make them sound human — not changing the words.



Where the script can't help you: everything a real client throws at you. A vague text with no context. A client describing a service using the wrong name. Someone who's hesitant but won't say why. Someone who asks about price before you've figured out what they actually want. There is no script for these. There's a framework, and there's your judgment.



This is the part people underestimate. A big chunk of this job is not reciting — it's listening to what someone actually means and figuring out the next move in seconds, while they're on the phone with you.



Scripts do change here, but only based on data. If you bring an idea for a better line, we'll A/B test it. If it wins, it becomes the script. What we don't do is let setters freelance changes on the fly, because then we can't measure what works.



If you want to be told exactly what to say in every situation, this role will frustrate you. If you like having strong structure AND room to think, you'll do well.



---



SCHEDULE (PACIFIC TIME — GRAVEYARD SHIFT IN PHILIPPINES)



All schedule references in this post are in US Pacific Time. Because PH is 15-16 hours ahead of California, each shift starts late at night your time and ends the following morning.

- US workdays: Monday through Friday

- US days off: Saturday and Sunday

- Hours per day: 8 hours of work + 1 hour of break (30 min lunch + 2× 15 min breaks, or 30 min lunch + 1× 30 min break — your call)

- Pacific Time (US): 7:45 AM – 4:45 PM PST



Philippine Time during US Standard Time (roughly November through mid-March):



Shift runs 11:45 PM – 8:45 AM PHT

- A US Monday shift = late Monday night through Tuesday morning your time

- A US Friday shift = late Friday night through Saturday morning your time

- Your days off in PH local time: Sunday and Monday (until your shift starts late Monday night)



Philippine Time during US Daylight Savings Time (roughly mid-March through early November):



- Shift runs 10:45 PM – 7:45 AM PHT

- Same day-shift logic as above — shift starts the previous calendar evening in PH



This schedule is FIXED. It's based on data showing when our booking demand peaks. If you need flexible hours, rotating shifts, or plan to hold another job during these times, this role is not a fit.

Please re-read this section carefully and make sure BOTH the standard-time and daylight-savings schedules work for you long-term before applying. The 1-hour shift twice a year is non-negotiable — it follows US business hours. Please make sure BOTH schedules work for you long-term before applying.



---



COMPENSATION



Base pay:



$900–$1,000/month (depending on experience), paid via Wise on the 1st and 15th of every month.



13TH MONTH PAY included — paid every December on top of your regular base, not restructured into it. Prorated in your first year if you start mid-year. Total annualized base compensation including 13th month: $11,700–$13,000.



Performance bonuses (uncapped, paid monthly):



- $3 per new client showed appointment

- $2 per existing client showed appointment

- $1 per rebooking confirmation (low-effort confirmation calls for clients who already booked through the salon)



Tiered cumulative threshold bonuses (paid monthly):



- +$75 at 90 showed appointments/month

- +$150 at 120 showed appointments/month

- +$350 at 150 showed appointments/month



Worked examples:



Baseline performer — 90 showed appointments/month:

- Base: $950 (midpoint)

- Performance: ~$225 (avg $2.50/show × 90)

- Threshold bonus: $75

- Total: ~$1,250/month



Solid performer — 120 showed appointments/month:

- Base: $950

- Performance: ~$300 (avg $2.50/show × 120)

- Threshold bonus: $225 ($75 + $150)

- Total: ~$1,475/month



Top performer — 150 showed appointments/month (90% show rate on ~167 booked):

- Base: $1,000

- Performance: $450 ($3×90 new + $2×20 existing + $1×40 rebooking)

- Threshold bonuses: $575 ($75 + $150 + $350)

- Total: ~$2,025/month



This is a PERFORMANCE-PAY ROLE. 30–50% of your monthly income should be earned through bonuses. The base is intentionally modest. If you want a high guaranteed salary with low expectations, this is not the role.



---



OTHER BENEFITS



1. Annual performance-based raise after your first year

2. 14 days of PTO per year, single bucket, available after 90-day probation (use for vacation, holidays, sickness — your call). For planned multi-day time off, give us at least 1 week's notice so we can plan coverage. Emergencies are understood — just communicate as soon as you can.

3. 90-day initial probation period. Pay is NOT REDUCED during probation.



To confirm you have read this post in full, include the word BURGUNDY in your answer to the final question on the application form



---



TARGET KPIs



- Lead to Booking Rate: 25%+

- Show Rate: 90%+

- Bookings per day: 4–9

- Showed appointments per month: 100–160

- Daily volume: Finish all assigned tasks each day. We supply ~17–25 leads per day plus follow-ups, no-shows, reactivations, and rebooking confirmations. HIGH CALL VOLUME (150–250 CALLS/DAY) IS NORMAL AND NON-NEGOTIABLE. If that sounds overwhelming instead of energizing, this is not a fit.



---



WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR



Background:



- Female candidates tend to perform best with our 35–65 female clientele, so we especially encourage strong female applicants — but the role is open to all genders.

- Bilingual (English + Spanish) is a plus but not required.



Non-negotiable skills:



The five that matter most — these are what we screen hardest for:



- Real-time thinking. You generate a good response in seconds, not minutes. Under pressure, with no script in front of you. This is the single biggest predictor of success in this role.

- Inferential listening. You hear what someone means, not just what they said. A client says "I need to talk to my husband first" — she's usually not asking for permission, she's telling you something about price or certainty that she doesn't want to say directly. If you take everything at face value, you'll lose bookings.

- Conversational initiative. You never dead-end a conversation, and you don't give up on a lead that's still alive. A client says "that's kind of far for me" — a weak setter says "no problem, thanks anyway" and loses her. What she's actually telling you is that she doesn't believe the drive is worth it yet. That's not a rejection, it's an assumption you haven't disproven. Answering someone's question is only half a response; the other half is the move that keeps things going.

- Rapport building. You can get someone to open up and feel comfortable with you fast. This is the biggest factor in whether someone books. These are emotional decisions, not logical ones. You don't need American cultural references — you need to make people feel heard, understood, and safe.

- Diagnostic reframing. You can say someone's problem back to them more clearly than they said it. When you do that, people assume you have the solution. It's the fastest way to build trust that exists.



Everything else:



- ADVANCED ENGLISH WITH MINIMAL ACCENT. An American listener should not need to strain to understand you. If we have to focus to follow what you're saying, that's a disqualifier.

- STRONG SPOKEN COMMUNICATION — CLEAR, CONFIDENT VOICE. YOU DO NOT RAMBLE. YOU ARE NOT SOFT-SPOKEN. If you fill silence with words because dead air makes you nervous, this won't work.

- Typing speed: 50 wpm minimum (65+ strongly preferred). You'll be taking notes and sending texts while talking. You'll submit a typing test screenshot with your application.

- Process discipline. Every call gets dispositioned correctly. Every lead moves through the right cadence. Every opportunity gets marked accurately in the CRM. This isn't optional admin — it's how we measure everything. Great conversations with sloppy process still means we're flying blind.

- Script discipline for the structured parts of the call.

- Natural call control. You can guide a conversation efficiently without talking over clients or letting calls drift. You redirect politely and keep the call outcome-focused.

- Sales experience: 6 months minimum (1 year+ preferred). Job-hopping resumes (multiple roles under 3–6 months each) will be disqualified.

- Comfortable holding the line on policies (rescheduling, deposits, etc.) without weakening the script or over-promising.

- Objection handling — you acknowledge, ask questions to reframe, and guide the client. You don't fire off rebuttals that invoke more resistance.

- CRM literacy. GoHighLevel experience strongly preferred.

- High data accuracy. You enter info correctly the first time. This is a precision role, not a speed-only one.

- Strong working memory and multitasking — you can listen, think, type, recall rules, and follow scripts simultaneously without freezing.

- Emotional steadiness under high-volume periods. Spikes happen. You execute calm under load.



Preferred:



- Familiarity with the salon/beauty industry

- Personal interest in beauty or self-care

- Experience working with older female clientele (35–65)

- Experience with Slack, Slite, Airtable, Claude or ChatGPT (we use AI to streamline daily work — if you can leverage it, you'll move faster)



Mindset (MOST IMPORTANT):



We'd rather hire someone who's a 10 in mindset and 7 in sales skill than the reverse. Here's what we mean:



- Ownership & volume mindset — you take responsibility for outcomes, not tasks. You see high-volume, repetitive work as leverage, not burnout.

- Process discipline — you operate consistently inside defined systems. You let your personality show through tone and warmth, not by changing the words.

- Sales psychology — you understand how to influence through trust, value framing, and subtle urgency. You communicate with intention, not chit-chat.

- Speed bias — you move fast, close loops quickly, and accelerate under pressure instead of slowing down.

- Coachability — you receive feedback without ego and adapt immediately. No defensiveness, no excuses.

- KPI awareness — you understand the numbers behind your role and how your daily actions move them.



---



TECH REQUIREMENTS



Non-negotiable:



- Internet minimum requirements: 50 Mbps download, 10 Mbps upload, ping under 80ms. Stable connection. We will test your speed and audio live from your actual work setup before we hire.

- Backup plan for outages. If your internet or power cuts out mid-shift, you need a real fallback — mobile hotspot, secondary ISP, UPS, co-working space, or some combination. You'll describe your specific backup setup in your application.

- Computer: 8 GB RAM minimum (16+ preferred). Processor: Intel Core i5 or equivalent, 8th generation or newer. SSD preferred. Working laptop or desktop

- Mouse

- Wired headset with boom mic (3.5mm or USB-C). No Bluetooth, no laptop mic, no AirPods.

- Webcam — laptop built-in is fine. You'll be on camera for interviews, training, and coaching calls.

- Quiet, dedicated workspace. No roosters, no karaoke neighbors, no babies crying, no traffic, no dogs barking during calls. We will hear it on the call, and so will our clients.



Preferred:



- Second monitor

- You already own a headset that meets the requirements above (we'll provide one if you don't, but having your own helps you start faster)



---



DO NOT APPLY IF:



- You struggle to think quickly and respond in real time. If you need a 
nt to figure out what to say, this role will be painful. Clients don't wait.

- You need the client to lead the conversation. If you're comfortable answering questions but not steering, this isn't it.

- You can't hold a conversation without a script telling you what to say next.

- You type slowly. Under 50 wp
ans you'll fall behind on notes and texts while you're talking.

- Your background is primarily customer service, general VA work, or admin support with no direct sales or appointment setting experience. This role requires proven experience persuading people, handling objections, and closing toward a booked appointment. Customer service experience alone is not sufficient.

- Your spoken English is hard to understand on the phone — this is a phone role first and the single biggest dealbreaker

- You're juggling multiple clients or planning to freelance on the side. THIS MUST BE YOUR ONLY JOB. We track performance closely and will discover this fast.

- You want a high guaranteed salary with low performance pressure

- You don't like high call volume or you find scripts "suffocating"

- You see remote work as "work whenever you feel like it"

- You can't sustain a graveyard shift long-term

- You're looking for a short-term gig — we expect a minimum 12-month commitment after probation



---



HIRING PROCESS



1. Application via Tally form (link below) — includes voice recording, Loom video, internet speed screenshot, backup plan description, and a few short written questions

2. 20-minute pre-screen call with our hiring partner

3. First-round interview with Ethan (~45 min) — includes live roleplay

4. Second-round interview with Ethan (~45 min) — final fit + offer discussion

5. Offer — targeting hires between August 10 – August 20

6. Paid training begins immediately after offer acceptance



---



HOW TO APPLY



Submit your application through this Tally form: | 
 |



IMPORTANT: There is a confirmation requirement embedded in this post. Applications that miss it will be skipped regardless of experience.



The form will ask for:



- A screenshot of your typing test results (
)

- A screenshot of your internet speedtest (speedtest.net)

title: Senior Backend Engineer / Technical Lead — Real-Time IoT Platform (Full-Time, Remote)
description:
A fast-growing health-technology company building a real-time IoT monitoring platform for senior care is hiring a Senior Backend Engineer to act as technical lead for a small, high-quality engineering team. Our wireless sensors run continuously in homes and care facilities, streaming event and vitals data over MQTT to our cloud. When someone falls, an alert has to reach a monitoring centre in seconds. Missed events are not acceptable, and we operate under strict uptime commitments to enterprise partners across the US, UK, Canada and Australia.



We have a strong in-house team but no senior technical leader who is close to the code. That is the gap this role fills.



What you will do



Review every pull request before merge. You are the merge gate and the standard-setter for code quality.

Run a short daily standup, keep timelines honest, and flag when work is slipping or an estimate is wrong.

Be the founder's technical eyes on the team: report on delivery, surface who is blocked, and recommend where the team needs to improve.

Own backend architecture for our real-time pipeline: MQTT ingestion, message brokers, event processing, and the path from device to alert.

Answer enterprise customers' technical and integration questions directly, within hours, so delivery never waits on the founder.

Work alongside a managed DevOps provider who owns infrastructure and reliability. You own whether the architecture is sound and product-safe; they own the plumbing.



What we need



10+ years building backend systems in production, still hands-on with the code.

Deep Node.js and MongoDB, plus real experience with message brokers (RabbitMQ or Kafka) and persistent connections (WebSocket or MQTT) under load.

You have built a system with many concurrent connections streaming continuously, and you remember exactly what broke and how you fixed it.

Strong code reviewer who can lead senior engineers through technical direction, not politics.

Can explain a technical risk or timeline to a non-technical founder in plain language.

IoT, real-time telemetry, or healthcare-adjacent experience is a strong advantage.



Nice to have, not required



Hands-on Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, or observability (Prometheus, Grafana). You will not own infrastructure, but you will work with the team that does.



How this works



Full-time, fully remote, one fixed daily standup slot plus flexible hours.

Direct line to the founder, no layers. This is a hands-on technical leadership role, not people management and not pre-sales.



To apply, answer both in your message



Describe one real-time or high-concurrency system you built. How many concurrent connections or messages per second, and what broke first when you scaled?

Single-instance MongoDB, 5,000 devices each streaming vitals every few seconds. What breaks first and what do you do about it?

title: SEO Specialist
description:
- Mission: Own SEO across Wolf IQ's Growth Plan clients and internal brands. You will run the content program, lead technical SEO, and be the person the business turns to when a search question comes up.

- Culture: High-performance, customer-centric, driven by data, design and collaboration. We value initiative, creative ownership and continuous learning.

- Location: Remote (Philippines-based). Strong preference for experience with, or awareness of, Australian and New Zealand digital culture and customer expectations.

- Reports To: Growth Manager



???? Why Join Us?

Wolf IQ is a profitable, fast-growing web agency helping small and medium businesses win online. Ten-plus years of steady growth, 500+ customers, and a Growth Plan program (SEO, Reviews, Google Ads) we are scaling from 15+ clients to 50+.

This is a role with a lot of surface area. You own SEO across 10+ active client accounts from day one, and you are the internal expert the rest of the business relies on. The playbooks, the reporting systems and the reusable AI skills already exist, so you are not building from zero. You are running a channel that works and making it better.

If you have solid SEO fundamentals and you have been waiting for a role where you own the outcome instead of clearing someone else's queue, this is that role.



???? What You'll Do as a Growth Engineer

Key Responsibilities:

- Own the SEO channel: 10+ active clients across content programs, technical SEO and local search. You set the direction on each account and you are accountable for what the client sees.

- Run the content program: Own the pillar article pipeline end to end - keyword and gap research, briefing, drafting, formatting, imagery, staging handover, and post-publish optimisation.

- Lead technical SEO: Site audits, on-page work, schema, redirects, indexation, backlink analysis and disavows. Using Semrush and the full Google stack.

- Talk to clients: Lead Growth Plan deep-dive calls. Present findings, defend your recommendation, and translate SEO into the things clients actually care about: leads, revenue, retention.

- Own the reporting cycle: Monthly SEO reports via Swydo, plus support on PPC reporting, complete before the 5th of every month.

- Be the internal SEO answer: When Sales, Support or Dev hits a search question, you are who they ask.

- Back up on paid: Google Ads sits with a dedicated specialist, but you will need enough Google Ads fluency to support reporting and step into an account when cover is needed.

- Systemise it: Find the repetitive work and remove it. Keep the playbooks current and document what is missing, so the process does not live in one person's head.

- Stay ahead of AI search: We are already working on answer engine visibility - structured schema, llms.txt, and content built to be cited by AI Overviews. You will learn it and help push it across the client base.



???? Who You Are

- 2-3 years hands-on SEO experience, with work you can point to and explain

- Solid technical SEO fundamentals: audits, site structure, redirects, schema, indexation

- Comfortable with content strategy, from keyword and gap research through to briefing and quality control

- Working knowledge of Semrush (or similar), GA4, Google Search Console and Google Tag Manager

- Able to explain your reasoning to a non-technical client without hiding behind jargon

- Organised enough to hold nine accounts and a hard monthly reporting deadline at the same time

- Proactive and responsive in a remote-first, async team. You ask early rather than go quiet



???? Preferred Qualifications:

- Knowledge of the Australian, US and New Zealand digital landscape and how local buyers search

- Google Ads exposure, enough to read an account and support PPC reporting

- WordPress, plus dashboard tooling such as Swydo

- ClickUp (or similar) for transparent task delivery

- Canva for producing article and campaign assets

- Practical use of AI tools (Claude, Gemini, Manus, or similar) to raise output quality and cut admin

- Local SEO and Google Business Profile management

- Any exposure to AEO/GEO and AI search visibility is a real advantage



???? Ready to Shape the Future?

If you want to own a channel rather than work a queue, and you want the room to grow into the strategy rather than just execute it, we should talk.



To confirm you've read the entire job description, please respond with the subject line: "Grow with Wolf IQ".

Be sure to include the following in your application:

- Resume

- A short note (3-5 sentences) on your prior experience

- One SEO result you owned end to end, with the numbers

- Photo of your work area

title: Full-Time Tiktok / UGC Editor
description:
READ THIS FIRST



This application requires a paid test video. It takes about an hour and I pay $25 USD for it whether or not I hire you.



Applications without a test video are deleted unread. Not set aside, not reviewed later - deleted. I've run this post before without the test as a hard requirement and got thirty applications I couldn't tell apart. I'd rather read five real edits than fifty resumes.



If that's not something you want to do, no hard feelings, but please don't apply - you'll be spending your time for nothing.



INTERVIEWS HAVE ALREADY STARTED. There is no closing date because there doesn't need to be one. I'm reviewing tests as they arrive and interviewing the strong ones the same week. The moment I find the right editor this post comes down. If you're reading this and you want the role, do the test today. Every day you wait is a day the seat is more likely already filled.



THE TEST



Folder (everything you need is in here):





Inside, you'll find the reference video, the raw footage, and a "Further Directions" file. Read that file before you start.



POSITION



Full-Time Short-Form Video Editor — $1,000+/mo — Established TikTok Pages (Long-Term Role)



TYPE / SALARY



Full Time · 5–6 days per week · PH or similar time zone $1,000 USD/month starting, potential for performance bonuses. Raises tied to skill and results.



JOB DESCRIPTION



I run TikTok pages that consistently reach millions of views. I'm looking for one editor to take ownership of the editing work alongside me, long term.



Success in this role comes down to two things above all else: editing quality and English comprehension. Because of that, this posting is specific about what the work requires, and the application asks for more than a résumé. I'd rather be clear upfront than have either of us discover a mismatch a month in.



THE WORK



Daily short-form vertical content — talking heads and voiceover/b-roll:



Cutting dead space so videos stay paced and never drag

Stitching the strongest takes into one seamless piece

Adding image overlays on screen to support what's being said

Zooms, crops, and reframes to keep the frame dynamic

B-roll builds: I provide a voiceover and footage, you find the visual that matches each line

Sourcing your own overlay assets — reading the script and independently finding the images it calls for



The last two items are the core of the role. The rest is technical work most editors can learn. Choosing the right visual for the right sentence is what separates a video that reaches 4,000 people from one that reaches 4,000,000.



SOURCING YOUR OWN ASSETS



This is one of the most important parts of the job, and the part most editors are not set up for. I'll give you background and direction, but I want you fully self-sufficient at finding the visuals a script needs. That means:



Reading the script and working out which images the moment actually calls for

Finding high-quality, aesthetically strong photos of the celebrities and influencers being discussed — not the first search result, but the image that looks right on screen

Learning the brands I work with well enough to represent them correctly

Knowing which parts of a brand's website are worth capturing, and pulling clean screenshots of them

Sourcing relevant comments, posts, and screenshots that support the point being made

Placing every asset at the right moment in the video, on the beat the script lands on



I shouldn't have to send you an image folder for a video to get made. You should be able to take the script and go find what it needs.



This requires genuinely understanding English — hearing a sentence and catching the humor, the tone, the reference — because you can't source the right image for a line you don't fully understand. Your English does not need to be perfect. It needs to be strong enough that you follow everything being said and that we can communicate quickly and clearly. Familiarity with internet and pop culture is a significant advantage here, and it's rewarded.



EXAMPLES OF THE WORK



Please watch all three before applying so you know exactly what you'd be producing.



Basic talking head — cutting dead space, piecing clips together, light crops and zooms: 

Talking head with overlays — the same, plus supplied images placed on screen: 

B-roll — a voiceover with footage matched to it line by line. This is where English comprehension shows most: 



WHO I'M LOOKING FOR

Strong attention to detail. You catch the frame held a beat too long or the overlay that sits slightly off. This is the most important quality in the role.

Self-sufficiency with assets. You can take a script and go find the images it needs without being handed a folder. This is weighted as heavily as your editing.

Willingness to go the extra step. Reviewing your own export once more and fixing what wasn't flagged.

Strong English comprehension. Understanding is essential; polished speaking and writing is a bonus.

Responsive communication. When I message during working hours, I need a reply promptly rather than the following day.

Exclusivity. This is a full-time position and I'm looking for someone working with me only — no other clients, agencies, or subcontracting. In return you get stability, a real salary, and an employer invested in your growth.

A long-term outlook. I'm hiring someone to grow with these pages over years, not to fill a short-term gap.



This role likely isn't the right fit if you're applying broadly today, prefer briefs explained in detail more than once, or intend to use AI to write your application answers — I'm looking for your own thinking.



REQUIREMENTS

Proven experience editing short-form vertical video (TikTok / Reels / Shorts)

CapCut or any software you work quickly in — the output is what matters

Confident sourcing your own images, screenshots, and reference material online, with good taste in what looks right on screen

Reliable internet and a computer that handles daily editing without issues

Available full time, with reasonable overlap with my hours. The volume moves with the content schedule — some weeks run 4–5 days, others run 6–7. I need someone who can flex with it rather than hold to a fixed number of days

Able to receive payment via Wise

Comfortable receiving direct feedback and applying it the first time

PAY AND GROWTH



$1,000 USD/month paid through Wise, with potential for performance bonuses. The ceiling on this role sits well above the starting salary — as you learn the pages and begin contributing your own ideas, your compensation grows accordingly. You'd be working directly with me each day on pages already reaching millions of views.



HOW TO APPLY



Subject line: EDITOR — [number of the example video above you think is hardest to edit] (For example: EDITOR — 2. Applications that don't follow this format won't be reviewed.)



Please include in your message:



Links to 2–3 short-form videos you personally edited, and what you handled on each. If you worked on only part of a video, please say so — accuracy matters more to me than scope.

In your own words, 3–5 sentences, without AI assistance: watch example #3 and describe one editing choice that worked well and one you would have approached differently. There's no right answer — I'm interested in how you evaluate a video.

The software you use and how long you've worked in it.

Your internet speed (a speed test screenshot is ideal) and your typical available hours in PH time.

One sentence on your current work and why you're looking to move.



Paid test — $25 USD. Shortlisted applicants receive a Google Drive folder containing the reference video plus the original voiceover takes and footage. You'll stitch together the strongest takes, match footage to the voiceover, and send back your version. Note that the folder deliberately does not contain every image the script calls for — part of the test is sourcing the missing visuals yourself and placing them where they belong. It should take about an hour. This test is paid $25 USD regardless of the hiring outcome — I don't ask anyone to work unpaid.



Google Drive (reference video and source files): 
/drive/folders/1En-NvVg9Fnfc7gdtdbv0xX5y4kAB-e5W?usp=sharing



A strong test is followed by a short call, and then a start date. I review every application that follows the instructions above.

title: E-commerce Operations & Customer Service Assistant
description:
We are looking for a reliable, hardworking **E-commerce Operations & Customer Service Assistant** to join our growing DTC e-commerce brand.



This is a hands-on role focused primarily on helping keep our day-to-day order operations running smoothly.



You’ll work closely with our customer service team and our fulfillment warehouse to resolve order issues, process returns, clear order holds, and make sure customers’ orders are handled quickly and correctly.



This role will start at approximately **2 hours per day**, Monday–Saturday. As the brand continues to grow, there is potential for the number of hours and responsibilities to increase.



We are looking for someone who is **fast, efficient, detail-oriented, and dependable**. You should be comfortable managing your own workload and getting through tasks without needing constant supervision.



## Responsibilities



Your day-to-day responsibilities will include:



* Liaising directly with our US fulfillment warehouse regarding order issues

* Reviewing and resolving orders placed on **fraud holds, address holds, or other fulfillment holds**

* Contacting or assisting our customer service team with orders that require customer confirmation before they can be shipped

* Following up on unresolved orders to make sure they do not sit on hold unnecessarily

* Processing customer returns and keeping return information organized and up to date

* Updating orders and customer information inside Shopify when required

* Investigating tracking, fulfillment, shipping, and delivery problems

* Communicating clearly and professionally with our warehouse team

* Maintaining a good working relationship with our fulfillment partners

* Communicating with customers when required and following our existing **brand tone and customer service style**

* Escalating unusual or more complex problems to the appropriate team member

* Keeping accurate records of outstanding issues and making sure they are followed through until resolved

* Identifying repeated fulfillment or customer issues and bringing them to our attention

* Helping improve internal processes and SOPs as the business grows



## What We Are Looking For



You must have:



* Previous experience working with an **e-commerce or DTC brand**

* Strong experience using **Shopify**

* Experience dealing with customer orders, fulfillment, returns, tracking, or similar operational tasks

* Excellent written English

* Strong attention to detail

* The ability to work **quickly and efficiently**

* Good organizational and problem-solving skills

* The ability to manage multiple small tasks without letting things get missed

* A proactive attitude - we do not want someone who waits to be told about every small issue

* The ability to work independently and follow established processes

* Reliability and consistency with working hours

* Professional communication skills when dealing with both customers and external partners

* The ability to learn and follow our brand's tone when communicating with customers



We are a growing brand, so things move quickly. We are looking for someone who is comfortable taking ownership of their responsibilities and making sure tasks are actually completed rather than simply passed on to somebody else.



## Nice to Have



Experience with any of the following would be a bonus:



* Shopify

* Gorgias, Zendesk, Reamaze, HelpScout, or similar customer service platforms

* Loop Subscriptions, Recharge, Skio, or similar subscription platforms

* ShipHero

* Working directly with US fulfillment warehouses or 3PLs

* Fraud review or address verification

* DTC beauty, skincare, wellness, or supplement brands

* Creating or improving SOPs and internal processes



We use **Time Doctor to track working time and productivity**.



## Working Hours



This is a **part-time remote position starting at approximately 2 hours per day, Monday–Saturday*.



You must be available during **US business hours** and able to work at approximately **the same time every day**.



Consistency is important for this role because you will be communicating with our US warehouse and resolving issues that can delay customer orders.



As our order volume grows, there is the potential for the role to increase beyond 2 hours per day.



## Pay



**$4–$5 USD per hour**, depending on experience.



There is potential for additional hours and greater responsibility as the company continues to grow.



## Who We Are Looking For



We are looking for someone who is genuinely hardworking and takes pride in getting things done properly.



You should be the type of person who sees an order on hold and wants to get it resolved rather than leaving it for tomorrow.



A lot of this role involves relatively simple tasks, but they are extremely important to the customer experience. An incorrect address, an unresolved warehouse hold, or a return that isn't processed properly can quickly turn into an unhappy customer.



We therefore need someone who is **organized, responsive, efficient, and extremely reliable**.



You will also represent our brand when communicating with customers and our warehouse, so professionalism and communication matter.



We want to build a long-term relationship with the right person and give them more responsibility as the business continues to grow.



## How to Apply



Please include:



* A short introduction about yourself

* Your previous e-commerce/DTC experience

* Your experience with Shopify

* Whether you have worked directly with a fulfillment warehouse or 3PL before

* Any experience handling returns, order holds, address issues, fraud reviews, or fulfillment problems

* The customer service and e-commerce tools you have used

* Your current time zone

* The exact hours you are available to work each day

* Your expected hourly rate

title: Closara: Cold Outreach & Demand Specialist
description:
Cold Outreach & Demand Specialist: Signal Research  ·  Cold
  ·  Direct-Response Copy  ·  Booking the Right Rooms



You can look at a company for ninety seconds and know the one line that’ll get a reply. Here, that’s the whole job.



Read this first — it’s the first test:

We could’ve written the usual ad. “Fast-growing company seeks motivated
 marketing specialist to join our dynamic team.” You’ve read that one four hundred times. So have the decision-makers we
 — which is exactly why we don’t send it, and why this ad reads like a person wrote it, not an HR template.



Here’s the honest version. This is one seat with one job: fill the calendar with the right conversations. Find the right person at the right company, work out the one true thing worth saying to them, say it like a human, and book the call. You don’t build funnels. You don’t run ads. You don’t wire automations. Someone else owns each of those. You own the cold open — and, in time, every word of outbound copy we send.



If you’re a generalist who “also does a bit of
,” this isn’t your seat, and the application below filters you out in about a minute. If you’re the person who gets a genuine kick out of pulling a 20% reply rate on a tight list of 200 while the industry average sits near 3 — keep reading.



APPLICATION KEY   Start your application with the word “COLD OPEN” and one sentence naming the best reply rate you’ve ever pulled on a cold campaign, and roughly how big the list was. No keyword, no read.



01   What Closara is (the sixty-second version)

Closara is the lead-to-revenue layer for sales-led businesses. In plain terms: we make sure no lead a business paid for ever slips through the cracks, and we place qualified demand with operators set up to take more of it. We’re Australian, we’re early, and we’re deliberately building this as a set of specialists who are each the best at one thing — not generalists who are average at five. You’d be the outbound one.



The founder (Sash) — and, as we grow, our closing team — runs every sales call and closes every deal. Your job stops at a booked, confirmed call in the calendar. You find them, you warm them, you book them. We take it from there.

We start with Australian homeowner verticals — solar and battery first, then the rest of the homeowner market. From there the map gets bigger: financial-services verticals as our legal clearances land, and other countries after that. The person who owns outbound while that map expands is the person who wrote the first cold
. That’s the seat you’re applying for.



02   What you’d actually own:

-The list. Not a bought blast — a tight, researched list where every single name has a reason to hear from us. High-ticket lead buyers in approved verticals (solar and battery first). You find the exact decision-maker and the signal that makes now the right moment: they’re running ads, they’ve posted a sales role, they’ve got a quiz funnel live, they just expanded. Signal-based, never spray-and-pray — because reaching the right person at the right moment is the difference between a 3% reply rate and a 20% one.

-The first line. The whole game. “Hi {first_name}” is not personalisation and hasn’t been for years. You open with one specific, true observation about their business that proves you actually looked. We have a house method for this — you’ll learn it and run it at volume without it ever reading like a template.

-The copy behind it all. You own the cold open (bespoke, per prospect) and the follow-up ladder (templated, written once per vertical, that the non-repliers drop into). As you prove the beachhead, you become the voice behind Closara’s own outbound and nurture copy too — same craft, same house voice. You write the sequences; our tech operator wires and runs them. The words are yours; the machine isn’t.

-The sequence. Multi-step, multi-channel —
 carrying the ask, LinkedIn carrying the recognition, the odd SMS. Two touches a week, no touch repeating an angle, every one short enough to read on a phone at a red light. Run off dedicated, warmed sending domains — never our primary.

-Deliverability. The un-sexy part that makes or breaks everything, and it’s non-negotiable knowledge. SPF, DKIM, DMARC aligned and passing. Spam complaints under 0.1% and never near 0.3%. One-click unsubscribe done properly. Warm-up, volume ramps, list hygiene. In 2026 a badly-run domain doesn’t land in spam — it gets rejected outright and never arrives. You protect our sending reputation like it’s your own money. It’s ours.

-The replies. You handle the back-and-forth by
 and DM with exactly one objective: a booked call in the calendar. Calm, quick, human. You never quote a price. You never negotiate. (More on that below — it matters more than anything else in this ad.)

-AI, used properly. You lean on AI hard — Claude, ChatGPT — for research, drafting and variants. But you have the ear to catch when AI sounds like AI, and the skill to prompt it so the output reads like a busy human typed it in under a minute. The market is drowning in obviously-robotic cold
 right now. That’s our opening: the interrupt is sounding real.

-A daily glance at the inbox (small, capped). Once a day, a quick look at DMs on the company socials and LinkedIn — flag anything that’s actually a buyer and pass it into the flow. That’s it. A ~10% side-duty, not a second job. The seat is outbound.



03   The part that makes this role special — you ARE the pattern interrupt:

Most cold outreach people never get this: in a market drowning in hype, the interrupt is understatement. In a market drowning in beige, the interrupt is warmth. You read the target’s inbox first, then you send the opposite of what’s already in it.

To show you exactly what we mean — and what bar you’re being hired to hit — here’s the same moment done two ways.

-What the whole market sends:

“Hi there! I hope this
 finds you well. My name is [X] and I’m reaching out from [Company], a leading provider of high-quality lead generation solutions. We help businesses like yours scale their revenue with our proven system. Would you be open to a quick 15-minute call this week to explore synergies?”



-What we send:

Subject: your quote form

Hey Dave — quick one. Your battery ad drops people on the homepage instead of a matching page, and your quote form asks nine questions. Homeowners bail around four. Free tip, do what you like with it.

While I’ve got you: I place exclusive solar leads, one business per lead, and I’m working out where the next lot should go. Reckon you might suit. Half an hour this week — Tue 10 or Thu 2?

Sash



One of those gets deleted. The other gets a reply. If you can feel why — the specificity, the value before the ask, the total absence of “synergies” — you might be who we’re looking for. If you’d have written the first one, you wouldn’t be happy here anyway.



Your job is to produce the second kind — every time, at volume, in the house voice, without it ever going stale. That’s a real skill. We pay for it and we take it seriously.



04   What you need

Must have:

-A real cold-outreach track record you can show. Not “I’ve done
 marketing.” A specific campaign YOU ran — the tool, the domain setup, the sequence, and the actual reply / positive-reply rates. Screenshots fine, redact whatever you need to. -First thing we look at.

-Deliverability fluency. If warm-up, DMARC and spam-complaint rate aren’t second nature, this isn’t your seat. We’ll ask, and we’ll know. A brilliant writer who’s torched a sending domain is worse than useless to us.

-Genuinely good direct-response copywriting. Short, specific, human. Send 2–3 cold
s you actually wrote. We’re reading for ear, not grammar.

-AI-native. You use AI daily to work faster, and you can make it sound like a person. You keep up — you know what changed this quarter.

-Enough automation sense to brief a builder. You don’t wire the automations yourself — we have a tech operator for that. But you understand the workflow well enough to spec it and hand it over cleanly. “I know what I want automated and I can explain it” is the bar, not “I can build it.”

-Excellent written English and a calm, human touch in replies.

-Full-time, single focus, AEST-overlapping hours. This is your one thing.

Bonus points"

-Deep with the modern stack — Apollo for data and sequencing, Instantly or Smartlead for cold send, and Clay for signal enrichment at scale. Say so loudly if you’ve run these in anger.

-LinkedIn outbound done manually and well — no banned automation; we don’t risk the founder’s account.

-You’ve booked calls for a founder-led sales motion before and know how to qualify without over-qualifying.

-You’ve worked a homeowner-services or high-ticket local-business vertical. 



05   The two hard rules — read these twice:

Break either of these and it doesn’t matter how good your reply rate is.

-Rule one: you never talk price. Not a number, not a range, not “it depends but usually around.” Our entire model runs on price being worked out live on the call, off the prospect’s own numbers. Your job is to get them into that room. The moment you quote anything, you’ve undercut the whole business. When they ask — and they will — you have one move: “That’s the call. I’ll get you in with Sash.” We test this in the application. A miss here is disqualifying.

-Rule two: approved verticals only. You work the GO list (solar and battery first; then roofing, HVAC, hot water, security, home improvement). Regulated verticals — mortgage, insurance, finance, property investment, wealth — are untouchable without written sign-off. Legal MVA / personal-injury / workers-comp lead work is never on, full stop. Not sure whether a vertical is approved? You ask before you send. Never guess.



06   The test — do this with your application

This is the real filter, and it’s deliberately harder than most job tests. A capable operator will enjoy it. Do all four parts:

1. Pick a real target and name the signal. Find a real Australian solar & battery installer in the Meta Ad Library. Tell us the one buying signal you’d lead with — and why that signal, over everything else you could have chosen.

2. Write the cold open. The first-touch
, under 80 words, subject line included, built around that signal. This is the only
 that’s bespoke, so it has to earn the reply on its own.

3. Write the follow-up ladder. Three short templated touches the non-repliers drop into after the cold open — the ones you’d reuse across every prospect in the vertical. Show us you understand the model: one custom open, a templated ladder behind it.

4. Show us the machine. In a few sentences: how would you build and enrich a list of 200 of these, at a reply rate you’d stake your name on — what tools, what signals, what you’d automate and what you’d keep by hand? And name the spam-complaint rate you’d never cross, and how you’d warm a fresh domain before any of this goes out.

Get part 4 wrong on the deliverability numbers and the rest doesn’t matter — that’s the tell between someone who’s run real campaigns and someone who’s only read about them.



07   The money — and how it grows:

We pay a modest base and real money on closes. You are not paid for booking a call, or even for a call that shows up — you’re paid when a client you sourced actually signs on and pays. That’s the only number that means anything to either of us, and it’s how a genuinely good operator makes this a well-paid seat.

-Base: US$600–900/month depending on proven depth, full-time, paid reliably.

-Close commission: US$200 for every new client you sourced who commits to an ongoing schedule and pays their first real invoice — not a test pilot. A tyre-kicker who takes a trial and vanishes doesn’t count; a committed, paying client does.

-Continuity kicker: a further US$100 if that client is still active and paying at 90 days — because we want you booking the right buyers, not just any buyer.

-Monthly accelerator: land 5 or more committed clients in a single month and you get an extra US$200 on top. That’s a great month, and it should feel like one.

-Where it heads: string a few closes together in a month and this becomes a genuinely well-paid seat. The better your booked-and-closed numbers, the more you earn — and this is the person who grows into owning outbound across every vertical we open, and writing the copy behind all of it.



What you could earn

A month where you…

-find your feet =  US$950

-hit your stride = US$1,550

-have a strong month US$2,350

*Illustrative, on a US$750 base; the strong month includes the US$200 bonus for landing 5 in a month. A strong operator clears US$25,000+ a year — and that’s before we open the next vertical and the next country, which is exactly where this seat is heading. The 90-day kicker lands about three months after a close, so it stacks as your book of committed clients grows.



How to apply

Send: (1) the keyword “COLD OPEN” + your best cold reply rate and rough list size; (2) a walkthrough of one real campaign you ran — tool, domain setup, sequence, reply rate (screenshots fine, redacted fine); (3) 2–3 cold
s you wrote; (4) all four parts of the test above; (5) a 60–90 second Loom introducing yourself in English; (6) confirmation you can work AEST-overlapping hours, full-time.

If your application starts with the keyword, shows a real campaign, and nails the test — you’re already ahead of almost everyone. Those things ARE the job.

title: Architectural Content & Community Coordinator – Residential Layout Design

title: Recruiting & Appointment Coordinator — US Roofing Company | $1,300/mo + Bonuses + 13th Month | Long-Term Full-Time
description:

ABOUT US



Trinity Roofing is a family-owned roofing company in Massachusetts, USA, run by a father-and-son team with over 17 years serving homeowners. We're not trying to be the biggest roofing company — we're trying to be the most trusted. We're building a growing door-to-door appointment program, and this role is at the center of it.
